html:
Company: Medicaments producer · Home country: France · Size: Small (<50 staff) · HS 300490 (Pharmaceuticals) · Trade data 2019-2024

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER. Attractive market with manageable risks.

Market attractiveness: 7.0/10
Recommended entry mode: Joint venture or licensing with an established Chinese partner

  • Import market of $15.12 bn in 2024, trend growth +1.7% a year (data confidence: high).
  • Supply is moderately concentrated (HHI 1,022); top supplier Germany holds 20.92%.
  • CAGE distance from France: high.
  • Applicable import duty: 0.45% (MFN rate (no free-trade agreement)); landed cost ≈ +12% over ex-works price before VAT.
  • France is supplier #6 with 6.7% of imports, priced mid-market (1.07x market average per kg).
  • EU-27 suppliers hold 62.24% of China's imports.

2. Market Size & Growth

Market size is measured as imports into China (UN Comtrade (China-reported imports, excluding re-imports of Chinese goods)). Imports show demand served from abroad, not total consumption.

Year Imports (USD)
2019 $14.80 bn
2020 $14.96 bn
2021 $17.11 bn
2022 $16.54 bn
2023 $17.71 bn
2024 $15.12 bn

Growth 2019-2024: trend +1.67% a year (log-linear fit over all years); end-point CAGR +0.43%.

Data confidence: High. No quality issues detected.

Market average unit value: $181.71/kg. Unit values show each supplier's price level (product mix also matters).

HHI 1,022: Moderately concentrated. Supply is reasonably spread, so there is room for a differentiated new entrant.

The EU-27's share of China's imports moved from 69.77% (2019) to 62.24% (2024).

Your starting position: France

  • Supplier #6 of 56 with 6.7% of imports in 2024 (-2.67 pp since 2019).
  • Price level: Mid-market, $194.00/kg vs a market average of $181.71/kg (1.07x).

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: One-party state with active industrial policy (Made in China 2025, dual circulation). Geopolitical tension with the EU and US; retaliation risk in trade disputes (e.g. EU brandy, pork, dairy probes).
  • Economic: World's second-largest economy and a huge consumer market, but slower growth, weak consumer confidence and strong price competition from domestic champions. Latest: GDP growth 5.0% (2025), inflation 0.1% (World Bank).
  • Social: Digitally native consumers; 'guochao' preference for domestic brands among younger buyers; foreign brands win on safety, heritage and premium positioning.
  • Technological: World-leading e-commerce and super-apps (Tmall, JD, Douyin, WeChat); fast product cycles; strong domestic manufacturing capability.
  • Environmental: Dual-carbon goals (peak 2030, neutrality 2060) drive demand for clean-tech; growing ESG disclosure requirements.
  • Legal: Foreign Investment Law (2020) improved access; still complex licensing, local standards (GB/CCC), data-localisation rules and uneven IP enforcement. Long, data-heavy approval processes; pricing set or negotiated by public payers.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural High Different language families (Romance vs Sinitic); localisation needed.
Administrative High No EU-China FTA: MFN tariffs, CCC/GB standards, distinct legal system and growing trade tension.
Geographic High ~8,217 km between capitals. Long lead times (Asia-Europe sea freight ~30-45 days; China-Europe rail ~15-20 days).
Economic High GDP per capita $48,986 (home) vs $13,862 (target), ratio 3.5x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

Import duty

  • MFN applied tariff of China: 0.45% (range 0-4% across 42 national tariff lines), 2023 (World Bank WITS / UNCTAD TRAINS (MFN applied, simple average)).
  • Likely rate for a company from France: 0.45% (MFN rate (no free-trade agreement)).

Indicative landed cost (per 100 of ex-works value)

Item Amount Assumption
Goods (ex-works) 100.00
Freight & insurance 10.00 10% for high distance
Import duty 0.49 0.45% on CIF value
Clearance, broker, port 1.50 1.5%
Import VAT 14.36 13% (China), usually recoverable for VAT-registered importers
Landed cost 126.36 112.00 before VAT (+12.0%)

Regulatory checklist

  • NMPA drug registration with local clinical data requirements; a Marketing Authorisation Holder or agent in China
  • Volume-based procurement (VBP) puts strong price pressure on off-patent drugs
  • Customs registration of the consignee; Chinese-language labelling for retail goods
  • Foreign Investment Law (2020) and the Negative List: most sectors open to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOE)
  • Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) for any customer data collected
  • Cross-border e-commerce (e.g. Tmall Global, JD Worldwide) allows testing demand under a lighter regime for many consumer goods

Official texts: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) · General Administration of Customs (GACC) · MOFCOM: foreign investment and the Negative List

Regulatory notes compiled 2026-11-21 from official sources; not legal advice.

Verify current duties and requirements: - China Customs tariff and regulations (GACC) - MOFCOM trade remedy notices - EU Access2Markets: China export requirements - EU SME Centre (China market guides)

7. Risk Matrix

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor Medium High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Long regulatory approval / registration timeline High High Start registration early with a local regulatory agent; budget 6-24 months.
Institutional and IP-protection risk Medium High Register trademarks and patents locally before entry; use contracts with local arbitration (e.g. CIETAC/HKIAC).
Logistics disruption (Red Sea, port congestion, freight-rate swings) Medium Medium Use mixed sea/rail routing, safety stock in a regional hub, Incoterms that share freight risk.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY/USD) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Joint venture or licensing with an established Chinese partner

  • Regulated sector: registration, distribution and hospital access depend on local relationships.
  • A partner shares regulatory and market risk while you keep IP protected by contract.
  • Your home country already supplies 6.7% of this market (rank 6): existing importers and logistics routes lower the cost of entry, so partner with established importers first.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 7.0/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 4.8/10, company size small (<50 staff).

9. Attractiveness Score Breakdown

Component Weight Score
Market size 25% 8.4/10
Growth 25% 5.6/10
Competitive openness 20% 9.0/10
Institutional quality 15% 4.8/10
Logistics 15% 6.8/10

Sensitivity to the weights

The weights are a judgement call, so the same sub-scores are re-weighted under alternative schemes:

Weighting scheme Score
Base case 7.0
Equal weights 6.9
Size-led (large incumbents) 7.2
Growth-led (start-ups) 6.7
Risk-averse (institutions first) 6.8
Niche entrant (openness first) 7.4

Robust: the score stays between 6.7 and 7.4, and the verdict band does not change.

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in China.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 1-30, registration: file the product registration / notification early: it is the critical path.
  4. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  5. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: joint venture or licensing with an established chinese partner.
  6. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.

Sources

  • UN Comtrade (China-reported imports, excluding re-imports of Chinese goods), trade data 2019-2024
  • World Bank WITS / UNCTAD TRAINS (MFN tariffs)
  • World Bank World Development Indicators, Logistics Performance Index, Worldwide Governance Indicators
  • Regulatory notes: curated from official EU and Chinese sources; verify with the links in section 6
  • Frameworks: PESTEL; CAGE distance (Ghemawat, 2001); HHI bands (US DOJ/FTC 2023); entry-mode logic (Dunning's OLI, transaction-cost theory)
